nodes.description: The cortico-thalamo-cortical loop generates sleep spindles and, when hypersynchronous, spike-wave discharges. GluA4 is the main fast AMPA subunit at cortical synapses onto inhibitory reticular thalamic neurons. In Gria4-deficient mice that synapse is weakened, synaptic responses are prolonged, and spike-wave discharges with behavioural arrest appear. For the human disorder this node is an extrapolation from the mouse: the patient alleles are heterozygous missense changes of unknown direction, not null alleles, though the human EEG findings (generalized spike-wave in sleep, ESES) are of the type the node predicts.

This is a single case and follows standard ESES practice rather than anything specific to GRIA4.

nodes.description: Receptors containing the mutant GluA4 subunit are predicted to gate or conduct abnormally. The SYTANLAAF motif couples ligand binding to channel opening, and the extracellular p.Arg697Pro variant may instead interfere with subunit assembly. Whether the net effect is gain or loss of current is not known for any GRIA4 patient variant; across GRIA1-4 patient variants, measured changes include agonist potency, response time course, desensitization and surface expression.

nodes.description: A de novo heterozygous missense change in GRIA4 at 11q22 is the initiating lesion. Four of the five original variants (p.Thr639Ser, p.Asn641Asp, p.Ala643Gly, p.Ala644Val) and the later p.Ala640Ser lie in the SYTANLAAF motif of the M3 transmembrane helix, the gate of the channel; p.Arg697Pro lies in an extracellular domain and p.Thr292Ser in the amino-terminal region. No truncating or copy-number allele has been reported.
